context: Decision first (w0). If fixing: move set/save so the secret is only persisted after validation succeeds, across the prompt-based setups that share the pattern; keep non-secret fields (host/port/database) savable on failure so retry UX stays pleasant.
description: Found 2026-07-31 during the credential-egress review. benchbox/platforms/credentials/singlestore.py collects the password via prompt_secure_field (:96), stores it in the credential manager BEFORE validating (:118), and then calls save_credentials() on BOTH branches - success (:124) and validation FAILURE (:134) - so a mistyped or wrong password is persisted to ~/.benchbox/credentials.yaml flagged INVALID. The prompt also seeds from the previously stored plaintext (:66). Contrast: the motherduck credential flow deliberately never persists its token (credentials/motherduck.py docstring and :70-74). This may be intended retry UX - w0 is a genuine decision point. If persisting invalid credentials is intended, document it in the module docstring and close; if not, only persist after successful validation. Check whether the other prompt-based platform setups (postgresql-family, clickhouse, starrocks, doris) share the pattern before fixing just one.
